title: TEAM Linhas Aéreas 6865

agencies.name: Centro de Investigação e Prevenção de Acidentes Aeronáuticos

summary: TEAM Linhas Aéreas Flight 6865, a Let L-410, crashed into Pico da Pedra Bonita on March 31, 2006, during a VFR approach. The crew cancelled their IFR flight plan and switched to VFR flight while the visibility was limited and weather conditions were poor. As the aircraft descended to 2,000 feet, it struck the mountain with all 19 people on board killed.
probable_cause: The crash was caused by controlled flight into terrain resulting from pilot error. The crew switched from IFR to VFR operations with inadequate visibility and were not aware of weather conditions and terrain in the approach area. The crew was not properly trained for the situation encountered.

factors.evidence: The visibility at the time was not good enough for a VFR approach
As bad weather approached, the crew descended to 2,000 ft when the terrain was higher
The crew was not properly trained, which caused them to fly at a lower altitude than a safe limit
The aircraft struck tree tops and slammed into the top of Pico da Pedra Bonita

events.text: The flight took off from Macaé at 17:19 local time operating under IFR
The crew cancelled their IFR flight plan and stated their intention to continue the flight under visual flight rules
As bad weather approached, the crew descended to 2,000 ft
The aircraft struck tree tops and slammed into the top of Pico da Pedra Bonita near the municipality of Rio Bonito

title: Armavia 967

agencies.name: Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety

summary: Armavia Flight 967 was attempting a go-around following its first approach to Sochi airport at night with weather below landing minimums. While performing the climb with the autopilot disengaged, the captain made nose-down control inputs due to loss of pitch and roll awareness. The insufficient pitch-control inputs led to failure to recover the aircraft and it crashed into the sea. All 113 aboard were killed.
probable_cause: The captain, being in a psychoemotional stress condition, made nose-down control inputs due to the loss of pitch and roll awareness while performing the climb after an aborted approach. The first officer's lack of monitoring the aircraft's pitch attitude and altitude, and no proper reaction to GPWS warnings, contributed to the crash.

factors.evidence: The captain lost pitch and roll awareness while performing the climb with autopilot disengaged.
The captain made nose-down control inputs due to loss of pitch and roll awareness.
The first officer failed to monitor the aircraft's pitch attitude, altitude, and vertical speed.
There was no proper reaction by the crew to GPWS warnings.
The aircraft crashed into the sea while conducting a climbing maneuver after an aborted approach.

events.text: The airplane took off from Zvartnots airport at 20:47 with 113 occupants on board
Crew decided to continue the flight to Sochi airport at 21:31
Crew reported gear down and ready for landing, then performed go-around after overshooting the runway extended centreline
During climb with autopilot disengaged, captain made nose-down control inputs due to loss of pitch and roll awareness
GPWS warnings sounded during the climb
The aircraft crashed into the sea after the crew's insufficient pitch-control inputs led to failure to recover

title: S7 Airlines 778
summary: Airbus A310 overran the runway during landing at Irkutsk after the captain unintentionally moved the left engine throttle lever forward while attempting to reduce reverse thrust on the right engine. The first officer, distracted by a spurious takeoff warning, failed to monitor engine parameters and did not detect the error until insufficient runway remained to stop. The aircraft crashed through the airport's concrete perimeter fence, struck rows of private garages, and burst into flames. The investigation concluded pilot error was the cause, with inadequate crew coordination enabling the control error to progress to runway overrun.
probable_cause: The captain inadvertently moved the left engine throttle forward while reducing the right engine's reverse thrust, causing the left engine to produce significant forward thrust instead of reverse thrust. The first officer failed to monitor engine parameters and did not detect the error. The crew's poor coordination resulted in inability to resolve the issue before overrunning the runway.

factors.evidence: Captain unintentionally moved the left engine throttle lever forward while attempting to reduce the right engine's reverse thrust.
Co-pilot failed to monitor engine parameters and was distracted by spurious takeoff warning on ECAM display.
Crew failed to realize the source of the problem and were unable to resolve the issue once the engine thrust configuration error occurred.
Aircraft overran the runway with only 800 meters remaining of runway asphalt remaining.
Aircraft burst into flames after crashing through perimeter fence and striking garages.

events.text: Aircraft touches down on runway, captain arms spoilers and engages autobrake to low mode, right engine reverser deployed to maximum.
Spurious takeoff warning alert appears on ECAM cockpit display during landing roll.
First officer attempts multiple times to erase spurious warning from ECAM cockpit monitor, becoming distracted from monitoring engine parameters.
While reducing right engine reverse thrust, captain unintentionally moves left engine throttle lever forward.
Left engine produces significant forward thrust instead of reverse thrust, aircraft begins accelerating instead of decelerating.
Captain notices aircraft did not slow down and asks first officer about RPM increasing and what is happening.
Captain orders right engine thrust reverser deployed again to maximum, but only 800 meters of runway remaining.
Aircraft overruns runway end, crashes through concrete perimeter fence, strikes rows of garages, and bursts into flames.

title: PIA 688
summary: Flight 688 took off from Multan with an engine that had been improperly assembled. At 60-70 knots, a pump malfunctioned and the aircraft veered right. At 120 knots the crew crossed V1 and elected to continue the takeoff despite being able to stop. The right engine flamed out after liftoff. The aircraft reached only 150-160 feet, entered an aerodynamic stall, and crashed into a mango garden.
probable_cause: One engine started to malfunction during the take-off roll due to improper assembly. Despite the aircraft being able to stop within the remaining runway distance, the pilots opted to continue their take-off, failed to carry out the correct emergency procedure, and the aircraft stalled from airspeed decay.

factors.evidence: One of the engines started to malfunction during the take-off roll due to improper assembly
The right engine suffered a flame out and began to spool down
The pilots opted to continue their take-off and failed to carry out the correct emergency procedure
The aircraft reached a maximum height of 150-160 ft and then stalled
Aircraft stalled and banked heavily, plunging onto a nearby mango garden

events.text: Flight 688 cleared to takeoff from Multan
At 60-70 knots during takeoff roll, pump malfunctioned
Aircraft veered to the right at 90 knots with decreased torque on right engine
At 120 knots, crossed V1 speed and cockpit crew decided to continue the takeoff
Aircraft lifted off and autofeather system activated; right engine flamed out
Aircraft reached a maximum height of 150-160 ft and then stalled
Aircraft banked heavily, plunging onto a nearby mango garden

title: Pulkovo Aviation Enterprise 612
summary: Tu-154M departed Anapa and half an hour later encountered severe thunderstorms and turbulence in the vicinity while en route to Saint Petersburg. At 15:33, the crew requested and received permission to climb to 39,000 feet. At 15:35:02, the crew disengaged the autopilot during high-altitude flight. Almost immediately, the stall warning sounded with the angle of attack increasing to 46 degrees while forward airspeed dropped to zero. The aircraft entered a deep stall with pitch oscillations exceeding operational range limits from which the crew could not recover. The flight crashed 45 km northwest of Donetsk near the village of Sukha Balka killing all 170 people on board.
probable_cause: Aircraft flown in manual flight mode at high altitude with excessive angles of attack causing a stall with transition to flat spin. Flight manual and crew training programs did not provide instruction on manual pitch control and pitch trim during high-altitude flight. Lack of appropriate high-altitude stall recovery simulators contributed to crew's inability to recover from the stall.

factors.evidence: stall warning sounded and flight's angle of attack increased to 46 degrees while forward airspeed dropped to zero

Flight manual and crew training programs did not provide instruction on manual pitch control and pitch trim during high-altitude flight and the lack of appropriate simulators contributed to crew inability
there were thunderstorms in the vicinity of the flight and the aircraft entered an area of severe turbulence
while avoiding areas of thunderstorms and turbulence the crew allowed the aircraft to enter pitch oscillations exceeding the angle of attack operational range
poor crew resource management allowed the situation to escalate into a catastrophic one
aircraft entered deep stall and transitioned to flat spin from which the crew could not recover and collided with ground at high vertical speed

title: Comair 5191

location.name: Blue Grass Airport, Fayette County, Kentucky

summary: Flight 5191 was assigned Runway 22 for takeoff but the captain taxied onto Runway 26 instead, which was only 3,501 feet long, unlit and unauthorized for commercial use. The crew conducted non-essential conversation during taxi resulting in loss of positional awareness. Despite the first officer noting the lack of lighting, the crew continued the takeoff. The aircraft accelerated to 137 knots but could not become airborne. The aircraft struck a low earthen wall, clipped the airport perimeter fence, and crashed into trees 1,800 feet from the runway end, destroying the aircraft. Forty-nine of 50 occupants were killed; the first officer was the sole survivor.
probable_cause: The flight crew members' failure to use available cues and aids to identify the airplane's location on the airport surface during taxi and their failure to cross-check and verify that the airplane was on the correct runway before takeoff. Contributing factors were the flight crew's nonpertinent conversations during taxi, which resulted in a loss of positional awareness, and the FAA's failure to require that all runway crossings be authorized only by specific air traffic control clearances.

factors.evidence: After confirming the takeoff clearance for Runway 22, the captain taxied onto Runway 26, which was only 3,501 feet long
The crew failed to use available cues and aids to identify the airplane's location on the airport surface
The crew engaged in nonpertinent conversations during taxi, which resulted in a loss of positional awareness

The crew failed to cross-check and verify that the airplane was on the correct runway before takeoff; when the first officer remarked about the lack of lighting on Runway 26, the captain agreed but did not abort
The aircraft reached the end of Runway 26 before becoming airborne, struck a low earthen wall, clipped the perimeter fence, and crashed into trees

events.text: Flight 5191 received takeoff clearance for Runway 22; approximately one hour before daybreak
Captain Clay taxied onto Runway 26 instead of assigned Runway 22; crew engaged in nonpertinent conversation

title: Gol Transportes Aéreos 1907

agencies.name: Centro de Investigacao e Prevencao de Acidentes Aeronauticos

summary: Gol Transportes Aereos Flight 1907, a Boeing 737-800 flying from Manaus toward Brasilia and Rio de Janeiro, collided almost head-on with an Embraer Legacy 600 business jet at 37,000 ft over Mato Grosso, Brazil, on 29 September 2006, killing all 154 aboard the 737. The Legacy's winglet sliced off about half of the 737's left wing, sending it into a nosedive, an uncontrollable spin, and an in-flight breakup, while the damaged Legacy made an emergency landing at Cachimbo Airport with no injuries. CENIPA found the collision was caused by ATC errors combined with the Legacy crew's failure to notice their TCAS had been disabled, while the NTSB held that both crews had acted properly after being placed on a collision course by ATC.
probable_cause: CENIPA attributed the collision to air traffic control errors combined with the Legacy crew's failure to recognize that its TCAS had been disabled, while the NTSB found both flight crews acted properly and had been placed on a collision course by ATC, treating the disabled TCAS as only a contributing factor.

factors.evidence: The Legacy crew testified they were cleared to flight level 370 by Brasilia ATC and remained level at that assigned altitude when the collision occurred.
CENIPA found the Legacy pilots failed to recognize that their traffic collision avoidance system (TCAS) was not activated.
The Legacy's left winglet sliced off about half of the 737's left wing when the aircraft collided almost head-on at 37,000 ft.
The 737 began to nosedive and enter an uncontrollable spin, quickly leading to an in-flight breakup.

events.text: The Embraer Legacy 600 departed Sao Jose dos Campos at 14:51 BRT on a delivery flight, cleared to flight level 370 by Brasilia ATC.
Gol Flight 1907, a Boeing 737-800, departed Manaus at 15:35 BRT bound for Brasilia and Rio de Janeiro on the opposite heading.
At 16:56:54 BRT the 737 and the Legacy collided almost head-on at 37,000 ft near the town of Matupa; the Legacy's winglet sliced off half the 737's left wing.
The 737 began to nosedive and enter an uncontrollable spin leading to an in-flight breakup; its CVR cut off at 16:57:47 after losing electrical power.
Despite serious damage to its left wing and tail and a disengaged autopilot, the Legacy crew landed the crippled jet safely at Cachimbo Airport.

notes: Record covers the Gol 737 that was destroyed; the Legacy 600 landed safely with its 7 occupants uninjured

title: Atlantic Airways 670
summary: Atlantic Airways Flight 670 overran the runway at Stord Airport on October 10, 2006 when spoilers failed to deploy, causing inefficient braking. When the captain selected emergency braking, the anti-lock braking system was disabled, locking brakes completely, causing reverted rubber hydroplaning on the damp runway. The aircraft fell down the steep cliff at runway end, killing four of 16 people on board.
probable_cause: Spoiler malfunction preventing lift dump, combined with emergency brake selection disabling anti-lock braking system, resulting in hydroplaning and runway overrun.

factors.evidence: the spoiler indicator light had not switched on
the damp runway surface and tires became extremely hot due to frictional forces
the commander moved the brake lever to emergency, disconnecting the anti-lock
the aircraft had insufficient speed to abort the landing and overran the runway

events.text: The aircraft touched down at 07:32:14 with slightly high speed at 120 kn.
The first officer called for the arming of the spoilers one second after touchdown.
The first officer called no spoilers as the spoiler indicator light had not switched on.
The commander moved the brake lever to emergency brake, disconnecting the anti-lock braking system.
Aware that the aircraft most likely would overrun, the commander attempted to reduce speed by skidding the aircraft, but it ran off the runway.

title: ADC Airlines 53
summary: Boeing 737-200 crashed into cornfield shortly after takeoff from Abuja in unsuitable weather. Aircraft encountered headwind-shift-to-tailwind windshear. Captain pulled nose to 30-35 degrees pitch angle while first officer requested more pitch. High pitch disrupted airflow to engines causing compressor stall in both engines and aerodynamic stall followed by left roll exceeding 90 degrees.
probable_cause: Pilot decision to take off in unsuitable weather with windshear present, inadequate windshear recovery training, and inappropriate control inputs during the emergency resulting in compressor stall and aerodynamic stall.

factors.evidence: Immediately after takeoff from Runway 22, the Boeing 737 entered into a headwind-shift-to-tailwind windshear
rotation was initiated at 143 kn and the aircraft then reached a peak speed of 162 kn before it started to decay
the nose rose further, reaching an angle of 30-35 degrees
inadequate company oversights on windshear recovery training
both engines to experience compressor stall
the aircraft lost its thrust, causing it to enter an aerodynamic stall
followed by a roll to the left of over 90 degrees and a steep descent into the ground
